original_intent.author: project-owner
original_intent.text: A fine-art editorial image about identity dissolving into material. A human presence that exists only as a reflection or contour on liquid chrome or brushed steel, in a cold industrial space under hard directional light. It should feel like the metal remembers a person who is no longer there: sculptural curvature, reflective titanium, quiet tension between the body and the surface. No faces, no robots, no sci-fi.

open_questions: Should the human figure be visible, partial, or only implied?
system_interpretation.summary: Offline keyword interpretation of the brief: engineered permanence; facelessness; identity as surface; industrial endurance; industrial perfection; industrial space; instability and flux; reflection and self-recognition; the body as material.

tensions.description: Default tension of the metallic editorial domain.
